for all its technical problems, i have some fond memories of Shadowbane

Ultima Online.

I put a decade into that game between official and player ran shards. The freedom of action pre-Trammel and the way character skills worked always appealed to me. The housing system was a major plus too. Everything from scarcity of land, watching IDOCs, and the benefits of ownership. It was a great housing system.

The game really lost a lot over the years. For years I enjoyed a player ran shard, but after it went belly up I never found the interest again.

I think MMOs tried to protect players from the actions of other players too much. That they didn't allow proper customization, leveling instead of unique skills. It seems EvE does these things right, but I couldn't get into it.

I tried WoW and Guild Wars 2 as well, but those didn't do it either. Now I'm into CS:GO mostly.
I used to play Ragnarok Online for many years until Gravity basically ran into the ground.
Glitch. It wasn't a combat MMO, but it was amazing.

Everquest. I don't think MMOs have failed nor we are not in a golden age. I feel like you cannot be lost in the world anymore, but that's mainly because there is so much convenience now. We have auction houses instead of staying in one map yelling our wares, you have fast travel instead of having to walk to each place. You have universal chat both in game on out (mumble, TeamSpeak, etc.). I'm grateful for these upgrade, mainly because I just don't have the time anymore. I have hundreds of games on steam to play and only an hour or two a night. I need something more bite size. Growing up sucks sometimes.

The star wars mmo was nice when it was first released but they destroyed that game in less than a year by dumbing it down and trying to appeal to the masses. I suppose anytime anything is mindlessly embraced by the masses or altered to cater to the masses the quality will be very poor.
Burning crusade or original WoW. I really hated it after that.

Star Wars Galaxies had so much potential. A sandbox game when it was first released similar in spirit to Eve. It was my favorite of the older games during that period. A player based economy where crafters made everything in game from resources gathered by players. Player created towns and military bases were the centers of the action. Skill based character builds where you could learn skills from other players and mix and mach skills you liked to suit your play-style. Open world opt-in PvP. We had some great town vs. town battles and rivalries.

Unfortunately, the game was completely mismanaged by SOE in an attempt to capture some of WOW's wider appeal. Wound up being a text book example of how not to treat your player-base by the end. I still remember the guy in charge John Smedley and I avoid anything he is associated with to this day. He was insulting and dismissive to the players who were upset after they made huge changes to the game overnight without warning.

I don't think the golden age is over. There is so much more variety of games out there now. There is more competition also and that is giving players more choices for what to play.

I think the downside is that the number of players is getting split between the games and it is harder for companies to support their games.

I still play EverQuest after almost 14 years. I'm a bit torn on the subject. I absolutely miss the way the game used to be, with amazing zone scenery, well crafted zones, interesting quests, a variety of enemy types, etc. I just DO NOT have time for the old school game anymore, but recent expansions suck ass compared to Kunark through Planes of Power. The Broken Mirror is a fucking joke. I fear that it might be the last expansion for the game.
